text: A matrix version is held on the `permission` rows themselves: `matrix_version` (DF-REF-044) is the label, the standard `state` column (TSD P4 v3 T3.0) carries the status of LOV-VERSION-STATUS, and this key's migration adds `valid_from`, `valid_to` and `approver_reference` to `permission`; no version table is created and an applied version is never edited.
why: `permission` carries no valid-from or valid-to date and no approver reference in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 while legacy AC3 needs an approved version with a valid from date, and the ownership map gives P4 no further table for the matrix.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.0, T3.1 (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044) and T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); legacy RWB-AD-002 AC3 and Data table; ownership map; DP-15.
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-access and the data steward
impact: The version travels with its rows, so a read needs no join and a second version carries its own dates; the approval stories update the state of the same rows and no other service is affected.

text: The matrix is loaded, read and versioned through four operations on `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin`: `POST /admin/permission-matrix-loads`, `GET /admin/permission-matrix`, `GET /admin/permission-matrix-versions/{matrixVersion}` and `GET /admin/permission-matrix-versions`, with Platform administration R for the three reads and C for the load, idempotent by Idempotency-Key on the load, and with no in-place update operation.
why: No source names the operations of the matrix: the ownership map and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A carry only GET /admin/roles (API-P4-007) and the reference-load paths, the legacy endpoint table names rule-version and reference-load paths that belong to other stories, and the sibling slice RWB-P4-E1037-CON already declares the generic role and permission read.
read: Ownership map (GET /admin/roles is P4's; the reference-load paths are P3's under ASM-A6-api-4); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005 to API-P4-008 and T6.1; legacy RWB-AD-002 Endpoints; Template and Rules §R4.
confirm: The solution architect and the security administrator
impact: The four paths are this key's contract and do not collide with `GET /admin/roles` or the reference-load path; a later change is additive within major version 1 and a breaking change is a new major version.

text: The rights of the matrix are Platform administration in TSD P4 v3 T6.1 — R for the three reads and C for the load, held by RW-SECADM (CRUDA) and RW-PLATADM (CRUD), with RW-AUDIT reading — and the legacy rows Reference data C for RW-COE and RW-REFADM and Rules and parameters A for RW-RISK are not carried.
why: The matrix is role administration and not reference data: `permission` and `role` are P4's under the ownership map, reference data is P3 rwb-case's, and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives RW-REFADM no right in Platform administration while giving the permission rows to the security and platform administrators.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1; legacy RWB-AD-002 Permission checks table and test case TC-AD-002-04; ownership map; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1 and VR-P4-004-2; DP-08.
confirm: The security administrator and internal audit
impact: The load is a role-administration act under the C letter; a role that needs it gets a `permission` row and not a code change, and the legacy Reference data row is recorded as corrected rather than as lost.

text: A load leaves the matrix version VALIDATED and this key stops there: the approval, the verify and the rollback of a loaded version are RWB-P4-AD010-APP's on the reference-load path, and the approver role of the `permission` table is read from the parameter `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM` rather than fixed in code.
why: The legacy criterion ends at waits for the application owner's approval, TSD P4 v3 T6.1 holds no application-owner role and no approval right for the `permission` table, and the Work Package assigns the approval step to RWB-P4-AD010-APP.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-002 AC1; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 and T4 (LOADED then APPROVED by a second person for a rule package); RWB-P4-E1037-APP precondition (`rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM`); DP-06.
confirm: The application owner and the tech lead of the approval gate
impact: The load and the approval are two acts with two owners, so a version cannot approve itself by being loaded; a new approver is a parameter row and no build.

text: A complete matrix holds exactly one row for every active `role` row of the environment against each of the 14 values of LOV-CAPABILITY, the expected row count is computed from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY and never written as a constant, and the labels `PM-2026.11` (in force), `PM-2026.12` (756 rows, validFrom 1 December 2026) and the refused `PM-2026.13` are the values of the criteria and of the tests.
why: The legacy criterion says a matrix file with every role and area and the sources fix neither the role count nor the row count: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 lists 42 role codes while the criteria of the same matrix count 54 roles and 756 rows, so a fixed count would refuse a correct file or accept an incomplete one.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-002 AC1 and AC2; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY with 14 values) and T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 field catalog and AC-P4-004-01; DP-07.
confirm: The security administrator and the data steward
impact: A role added by the role administration story makes the next matrix file one row longer with no code change, and an incomplete file is always refused with the gap named.

text: A matrix load publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with change kind `MATRIX`, the version label, the status VALIDATED, the effective date and the row count, after the commit; consumers refresh their cached permission data on it and then resolve the version in force on the date asked, so an unapproved version changes no answer, and whether the approval publishes again is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's call on its own path.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43 give rwb-access exactly two event names and slide 20 shows the estate refreshing cached permission data on AccessPolicyChanged, and no source says at which of the load, the approval or the effective date the matrix signal is published.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 43; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 (events: none); FSD P4 v3 A2.4; DP-14 naming; Template and Rules §R4.
confirm: The solution architect and the event platform owner
impact: One event name and one consumer signal; a refresh at a load is wasted at worst because the read resolves the version in force, and no consumer subscribes to a name that does not exist.

text: The matrix rows and versions are shown on SCR-43 Roles and access through the gateway-bff composite route, the legacy pair SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-40 Reference data is not served by this key, and the field list of SCR-43 and the place of the load form on it are the platform screen owner's.
why: FSD P4 v3 lists SCR-43 as the screen for roles, permissions, scope and the group mapping, while the legacy story names SCR-39 and SCR-40, which the rule-version and reference-list stories serve; no source fixes the layout of the load form.
read: FSD P4 v3 Screens list and A2.4; legacy RWB-AD-002 Screen and states table; DP-19; ownership map (no screen of its own).
confirm: The gateway-bff screen owner and the security administrator
impact: This key returns the rows and the versions only and the screen owner renders them; SCR-39 and SCR-40 stay with the stories that own their data.

text: The contract baseline fixes the field names, types and lengths of the four schemas, the error envelope and the additive-only change rule, and dictates no physical column: the valid-from, valid-to, approver reference and pending approver role are declared as fields of the version and their storage is the app story's migration.
why: No source defines the shapes of the matrix schemas and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 has no physical column for the version dates or the approver, so the contract must declare the answer shape while leaving the storage to the owner of the table.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2 and appendix T-A.1; Legacy RWB-AD-002 Acceptance criteria; Architecture v5 slide 42 (API versioning); Template and Rules §R7.2 s12.
confirm: The solution architect and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: The app story may add the physical columns without a contract change; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version.

text: The two stories and their contract baseline are used while they sit in Draft (realignment v1) under D-RCV-60 with no approval record, and the deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes stay open for the solution architect.
why: No human approval is recorded for this run (overlay of D-RCV-60), and no source fixes a deprecation window or a fake retention period.
read: Root AGENTS.md rules 1 to 14 and the D-RCV-60 overlay; Template and Rules §R1 U8 and §R9; Architecture v5 slide 42; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-B (DL06, DL11, DL26, DL35).
confirm: The solution architect and the governance lead
impact: The baseline unblocks Day-1 work and the two open values are recorded for the architect; no approval is claimed that does not exist.
